summary: Martinique Aimé Césaire International Airport (FDF) is the main gateway to Martinique, a French overseas department in the Lesser Antilles. Named after the renowned Martinican poet and politician Aimé Césaire, the airport sits on the western coast of the island near the capital Fort-de-France. It serves as the primary hub for both international and inter-Caribbean flights connecting Martinique to mainland France, North America, and neighboring islands.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Fort-de-France city center?
A: The airport is approximately 10 km (6 miles) southeast of Fort-de-France, with a typical drive time of 15-20 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Do I need a passport or visa to fly to Martinique?
A: Martinique is part of France and the European Union, so EU citizens need only an ID card. Visitors from other countries require a passport and may need a Schengen visa or short-stay visa depending on nationality.

Q: What airlines operate from FDF?
A: Air France operates the majority of long-haul flights to Paris, while regional carriers like Air Caraïbes, Corsair, and American Eagle serve other Caribbean and North American destinations.

Q: Are there duty-free shops at the airport?
A: Yes, the terminal features duty-free shops offering French luxury goods, Caribbean rum, local crafts, and perfumes, particularly in the international departure area.
transport_tips: Taxis are available outside the terminal and operate on fixed rates to Fort-de-France; confirm the fare before departure. Rental car agencies are located on-site and booking in advance is recommended, especially during the winter tourist season. The TCSP bus line connects the airport to Fort-de-France and other communes at a fraction of the taxi cost.
local_tip: If you have a long layover or early arrival, visit the nearby Les Trois-Îlets area just across the bay—it's closer to the airport than Fort-de-France center and offers beaches, the La Savane des Esclaves heritage site, and less crowded lunch spots.
